label: copy-phase input i fed back at recall positions 2-3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is the letter i (the model just output i) and the step is outputting original token 2 or 3, i.e. i was original token 1 or 2. It never fires on i in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token. Magnitude is strongest at recall_idx 2 (i was the second original token, e.g. y i 3 b ... <DEL> y [i]); there it carries about 70% of mass and nearly all top-quartile activations. recall_idx 3 is moderate, and recall_idx 1 and 4 give only rare weak activations. False positives are mostly short sequences (L=4) or i near the end of the copy. Restricting to L>=5 raises precision to 0.99 with little F1 change.

issues: Most of the original explanation holds up on the dev profile. The feature is active only in the copy phase (0 activations in the original and delimiter phases). It fires only when the input is i (100% of activation mass). By recall_idx, the mass share is 0.705 at 2 and 0.285 at 3, with only rare weak firing at 1 and 4. The reported test scores reproduce (P 0.899, R 0.933, F1 0.916).

There is a systematic false-positive class: the last copy step (to_go == 0). The predicate restricted to to_go==0 makes 2889 test predictions with precision 0.0. That is about 86% of the 3358 false positives. The feature never fires when i is fed back as the final output. Examples: 'x k i r <DEL> x k *i*' and '0 i g <DEL> 0 *i*'. The dev to_go profile agrees: 22 of 1M steps are active at to_go=0.

The explanation blames the false positives on 'short sequences (L=4) or an i near the end of the copy', but neither the predicate nor the label encodes this. The L>=5 fix it tried is a poor stand-in: test F1 0.920, and recall drops to 0.861. Adding to_go>=1 keeps recall at 0.933 and raises precision to 0.985, for F1 0.958.

After the fix, the remaining 469 false positives look like scattered noise (mostly i at recall_idx 2 in L=4-5 sequences). The misses hold only 1.0% of the activation mass and are weak (relative activations of 0.10 or less). Widening to recall_idx 1-4 drops F1 to 0.71, so leaving out 1 and 4 is correct.
